subject: Performance SLOs: p95/p99 latency – hosted vs current provider (recap & next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Ng <sara.ng@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLOs: p95/p99 latency – hosted vs current provider (recap & next steps)

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time to walk me through Finlytics' architecture and latency targets today. Below is a short recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can move to a short benchmark/canary with the Redwood hosted API.

Call recap (what I heard)
- Primary user flows: interactive analytics chat and real-time report generation (streaming responses for chat).
- Current provider (internal endpoints): end-to-end observed numbers: p95 ~ 180 ms, p99 ~ 420 ms (these are across your front-end -> provider -> model -> render path).
- Target SLOs: Finlytics would like to see p95 <= 120 ms and p99 <= 300 ms end-to-end to meet UX requirements.
- Concurrency & throughput: expected steady-state concurrency ~ 200-250 simultaneous active sessions, peak bursts up to ~400 concurrent; average request rate during peak ~50 req/s.
- Response sizes: average 120-200 tokens per response; streaming/token-by-token behavior is required for chat.
- Availability/SLAs: enterprise SLA and a predictable degradation policy are important.

What Redwood can propose (high level)
- Hosted API proof-of-concept: 1-week benchmark against a representative workload (streaming enabled) + short smoke test in your staging.
- Measurement plan: we’ll measure end-to-end p50/p95/p99 using your front-end harness (we’ll run tests through your staging URLs) and compare against your current provider.
- Typical optimizations we’ll exercise: continuous batching, KV-prefix caching, quantization profile aligned to your seq-length, and routing to lower-latency regions.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short Redwood performance sheet with typical end-to-end ranges and a draft SOW for the POC.

Next steps / asks
1) Please confirm the observed current-provider p95/p99 numbers above (or correct if I heard them wrong).
2) Can you share a staging endpoint and a short test harness (or allow us to run from our test runner hitting staging)?
3) Please introduce procurement/security contacts for the SOW and security questionnaire (if possible).
4) Proposed dates: run benchmark week of Mar 30 — are you available for a 30-min kickoff the week prior?

If that looks right I’ll coordinate with Aditya to scope the benchmark (concurrency/traffic shape) and with Neha on the SLO acceptance criteria and reporting format.

Thanks — looking forward to proving we can hit your p95/p99 targets.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs: p95/p99 latency – hosted vs current provider (recap & next steps)

Thanks Marissa — this looks like an accurate recap. A few clarifications and additional context: 

- Confirming current observed numbers (end-to-end): p95 = ~180 ms, p99 = ~420 ms. These include our front-end rendering and network overhead to the provider.
- Target: p95 <= 120 ms and p99 <= 300 ms would be ideal. We're willing to run some UX tolerance tests if we get close on p95 but still have some climb on p99.
- Streaming: required for chat. We need chunked token streaming (SSE/WebSocket acceptable) so users see partial output quickly.
- Concurrency: steady 200-250 concurrent editors/sessions during business hours; peaks up to 400 for certain jobs. Peak traffic shape includes short spikes (30-60s) where concurrency jumps and sustained periods of ~10-20 minutes at higher throughput.
- Throughput: average token output per request ~150 tokens; typical requests per user ~0.5-1 req/min during active sessions.

Procurement/security: I’ve looped in Jason Lee (cc'd) from procurement — Jason, can you help with the SOW and standard PO timelines? Our security team will want the standard questionnaire and confirmation that logs/audit events are available for the trial. 

We can give you staging endpoints and a small harness. I propose the benchmark week of Mar 30 is doable. For the kickoff — how about Tue, Mar 24 at 10am PT?

Sara
